answers.confusing_rules: 1) Fabricator: the rule says framing is free and forging costs a token, and both are actions on 'the chosen player'. It is unclear whether one Fabricator can frame one player and forge a different player's will on the same night, or whether doing both on one player counts as one visit or two. On N1 Dave did both on Alice, so I treated it as a single target with both effects, but the rule should say. 2) R8 Katana-holder disguise: the holder appears Not Evil to a Sheriff on the same night. On N4 Heidi was both the holder and Alice's investigation target, and she died that night, so I returned 'Not Evil' as R8 directs. It is correct by the rules but very counterintuitive, and nothing says whether framing would override it. 3) R16 end-of-day: 'anyone who was sent a private message during that round first gets one last turn' does not say whether that last turn may include public messages, which would restart the round, or whether a reply PM grants the original sender another turn. 4) Win attribution in R1: I awarded the win to dead Village members (Carol, Erin, Frank) because their faction won. 'A faction typically wins iff it has players alive' could be clearer that dead members share the win. 5) It is unclear whether a player who dies that night (Carol on N2, as Lookout) still receives their night result. I sent none.
answers.missing_information: No built-in state tracker. I had to track the following manually: token counts (Medic 2, Vigilante 3 then 2 then 0, Fabricator forge spent, Prosecutor and Clerk not in play), the current Katana holder after each vote and after Dave's death, which Yakuza voted for what, who was role-blocked (and therefore did not visit), and the full visit graph needed for Lookout, Tracker and Fortune Teller results. The visit graph was the most error-prone part: on N1 Carol watched Dave, and I had to remember that Alice's blocked investigation produced no visit, so the answer was 'nobody'. A per-night resolution sheet showing attacks against defenses (e.g. Katana Standard vs Medic Standard = fail) would help.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to run an automatic consistency check before sending results, for example: blocked actions removed from the visit list, defense compared against attack, and the Katana holder's disguise applied. I also wanted to use a structured notification template so messages are worded consistently. My N2 block message to Alice said 'last night' while the others said 'tonight'.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: No rule violations that I can find. Some outcomes look strange but are rule-correct. 1) Alice's only Sheriff result all game (N4) was 'Heidi is Not Evil' while Heidi was a Yakuza Grunt, because she held the Katana. 2) Erin and Heidi killed each other simultaneously on N4, which ended the game with Alice and Grace alive; the end check was done after simultaneous deaths as R1 specifies. 3) Erin's last will said she had 2 tokens left after spending them; this was the player's stale will, not an engine issue. 4) My message wording was inconsistent (role-block notices phrased 'last night' vs 'tonight'). 5) Dave's forged will only applies if the forged target dies, so the spent token had no effect; that is correct, but players may misread it.
answers.suggestions: 1) Give the moderator a live state panel: alive players and seat order, roles, tokens, Katana holder, active traps and doused players. 2) Auto-compute visits after removing role-blocked actions. 3) Clarify the Fabricator target rules, and whether frames and the Katana disguise interact. 4) Clarify the R16 last-turn rule. 5) State explicitly that dead faction members share the win and that players who die that night get no investigative result. 6) Provide standard templates for night notifications so wording stays consistent.

lessons.tip: Don't vote Guilty on a player just because they lack verifiable results; missing info from blocked nights is not evidence of guilt. Demand concrete reasons before voting, and be wary of a pair or trio pushing the same nomination.

Before a trial, agree privately with other Village members on a concrete test, such as which votes to watch and which dawn results would change your vote, so the village votes together instead of drifting.

lessons.tip: Treat each shot as a scarce resource: prioritize strong, converging evidence—such as a confirmed faction mate plus suspicious voting—over a single suspicious vote or behavior. Choose attack strength only as high as needed for the likely target and defense.

Separate facts from inferences. A role reveal or an independently confirmed action is stronger evidence than a pattern of private messages, a claim, or a vote; use those weaker signals to guide questions, not as proof by themselves.
Avoid publicly announcing future night targets. That gives opponents actionable information and can make your results easier to interfere with; share resolved results and feedback instead.
Compare voting behavior and explanations across players, but assess each person individually. Coordinated-looking votes are a useful lead, not automatic proof that every voter shares an alignment.
Keep discussion focused: once a point has been answered, seek new evidence or let the day move on. Repeating plans and arguments wastes turns and can expose useful information.

summary:
Village won despite the Yakuza having strong night tools. The Yakuza exposed themselves on Day 1 by forming a visible DM triangle. Dave sent Bob and Heidi repeated private messages, and Bob and Heidi then repeated his vague 'check-ins' explanation in public. That made all three the town's main lead for the rest of the game.

Alice claimed Sheriff and named her Night 1 target in public. Frank quietly protected her every night, which stopped the Night 1 Katana. Bob blocked her every night, so she got zero results, but the town still trusted her because she survived a Katana attack.

The Yakuza then pushed Alice to trial on Day 3 with no new evidence. All three voted Guilty together, and Heidi flip-flopped. Erin, the Vigilante, had held her shots for two nights. On Night 3 she used a cheap Basic shot on Dave, who had started the triangle and the nomination, and he flipped Fabricator. His fake 'Vanilla' will was shown to be a lie.

That flip let the town hang Bob, who also falsely claimed Vanilla. On Night 4 Erin spent her last tokens on Heidi and traded lives with her Katana, which won the game.

Notes on the Yakuza:
- They killed Carol (Lookout) and Frank (Medic) efficiently.
- They wasted Dave's forge token on Night 1.
- Heidi showed Not Evil to the Sheriff on Night 4 only because she held the Katana. That was irrelevant because Erin acted.
